sourceInformation.source: California Games (1988); the 1988 Amiga manual and original six-event format.
sourceInformation.perspective: Third-person 3D with event-specific oblique side views and a following course camera.
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 / r180 WebGPURenderer (WebGPU; built-in WebGL2 compatibility), Rapier 3D compat 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, ES2022; esbuild 0.28.2; AI Hub session client 1.4.0.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original procedural cel-shaded coastal diorama, ink outlines, apricot skies, teal water, coral and cream typography.
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframe tracks for pumping, cruising, pedaling, kicking and falling, plus procedural steering and aerial tricks.
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated 108 BPM surf shuffle, synthesized effects and Animalese-style gibberish; music defaults to 10%; no audio files.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub 1–2-player authoritative turn-based competition, dedicated host support, couch pass-the-pad duel, and explicitly labeled same-browser BroadcastChannel rooms.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless simulation, complete six-event and twelve-turn playthroughs, Chromium WebGPU, emulated standard controller, mouse/keyboard, touch stand-ins, offline PCM audio, file:// release checks, and official AI Hub latency/loss scenarios. Physical devices and listening: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: 1988 Amiga instruction manual, Sega manual, Epyx history, source screenshots and credits; six sports, trick timing, hazards, beach palette and chip-music character. Original release was 1987; 1988 source platform is inferred as Amiga.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu on WSL2.

testingFeedback: Testing and visual validation found 13 issues: 12 implementation issues and one environment launch-flag issue. All were corrected.
Two implementation issues were game breaking: footbag floor collision and generated HTML parsing. The supplied software-WebGPU adapter flag also destroyed the browser GPU device until removed.
The complete twelve-turn, two-player simulated tour was most helpful; it exercised all six sports, scoring, physics and event transitions.
A normal headless screenshot before verifying GPU survival was least helpful: it showed the UI but concealed the destroyed rendering device.
engineFeedback: Three.js native animation mixers, toon materials and geometry APIs made a cohesive procedural world possible in one HTML file.
Yes. HTML replacement-string expansion corrupted a bundled expression, and the supplied Chromium adapter flag destroyed WebGPU devices. Both were diagnosed and corrected.
The six distinct sports simulations, shared input and menu system, scoring and tournament flow needed to be built in application code.
Reliable WebGPU readback and software-browser verification were the hardest engine-related work.
none; no engine source was changed.
A built-in renderer health diagnostic with a reliable headless capture path would help.
promptFeedback: The concrete controls, attract mode, dev tools, sharing format and multiplayer acceptance criteria made the intended deliverable clear.
The 1988 source did not identify a platform, while California Games originally released in 1987. I used its six-event format and the 1988 Amiga manual.
Making six mechanically distinct sports feel consistent with a controller while packaging physics, animation, audio and multiplayer into one file.

Specify the source platform and clarify standalone internet networking versus local play. Update the software-WebGPU flags: use-angle=swiftshader worked here; use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader destroyed devices.

aiHub.name: Californiroll Games
aiHub.description: Ride a golden-hour tour of six coastal sports: half-pipe, footbag, surfing, roller skating, BMX and flying disc. Bank tricks and medals solo, pass the pad, or challenge a friend through AI Hub.
aiHub.controls: WASD/arrows or left stick to move; Space / Cross / A for the event action; Shift / Square / X for tricks; Escape / Options to pause; touch drag and contextual action.
